item.title: Cardinals found no loopholes versus Patrick Mahomes' loose cannon
item.description: The Arizona Cardinals defense had no chance of slowing down Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes and his immaculate entourage of skills players in Week 11. The 34-7 lashing at the hands of the Chiefs was practically a episode of pick-your-poison for Cardinals defensive coordinator Nick Rallis who was tasked with the responsibility of stopping the Chiefs multi-faceted offense. Rallis could only hope that the Cardinals offense would be able to conjure up a response to counter the Chiefs' offense Sunday. However, Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur and offensive coordinator Nathaniel Hackett were forced to rely on reserve quarterback Josh Johnson to decipher and dice the stingy Chiefs defense. Johnson produced measly results expectedly, averaging just five yards per passing attempt and the Cardinals offense had just one offensive touchdown in the loss. Also, the Chiefs offense had 72 total plays Sunday and this statistic is a direct result of six total punts by Cardinals punter Blake Gillikin. According to NFL stats, the Cardinals rank No. 4 in the league in punts per game, a point of reference for critics who shift blamed LaFleur's questionable offensive brilliance to veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett earlier in the season. Brissett has moved on with the Baltimore Ravens and yet LaFleur's offensive attack has still been pedestrian at best. Mahomes and the Chiefs totaled 435 total yards on offense in Sunday's win which mathematical means they yielded an average of six yards per play in their Week 11 win. Rallis can't continue to save the franchise from a continuance of horrid offensive play. Still, considering the level of competition within the NFC West and competent opponents on the Cardinals' schedule for the remainder of the season, it's about time to hold LaFleur accountable. LaFleur needs to prove his offensive prowess by producing first downs and touchdowns, and while injuries do play a factor, the statistical facts show that LaFleur has been less than fantastic. item.title: Why Is Victor Wembanyama Not Playing Tonight Against Kings? Latest Intel On Spurs’ Injured Players
item.description: Nov 21, 2026; San Antonio, Texas, USA; San Antonio Spurs forward Victor Wembanyama (1) looks up in the second half against the New Orleans Pelicans at Frost Bank Center. Mandatory Credit: Daniel Dunn-Imagn Images The San Antonio Spurs are severely shorthanded tonight as they have also ruled out two key players, Victor Wembanyama and De’Aaron Fox , for tonight’s regular-season game against the Sacramento Kings at the Golden 1 Center. Victor Wembanyama (back tightness) and De’Aaron Fox (Shin contusion) now join Dylan Harper , Tobias Harris , and Jayden Quaintance on the list of players sidelined with injuries. They both last played in the Spurs’ 114-91 win over the Pelicans on Saturday, November 21. “No Victor Wembanyama or De’Aaron Fox tonight in Sacramento, per source. Both are out with what can be described as bumps and bruises. Both are likely to return for Wednesday’s NBA Cup game in Portland,” Jeff McDonald of the San Antonio Express-News reported . Fortunately, this is not expected to be a long-term absence for Victor Wembanyama, who is among the favorites to win the Michael Jordan regular-season MVP award this season. He is currently averaging 29.9 points, 12.3 rebounds, 3.2 assists, and 3.9 blocks per game while shooting 54.1% from the field and 31.5% from behind the three-point line. While Wembanyama’s absence will already be a major setback for the Spurs, having De’Aaron Fox join Dylan Harper on the sidelines means all the primary backcourt responsibilities, like slashing and playmaking, will now fall on Stephon Castle . Stephon Castle will likely also shoulder a greater offensive burden, while the Spurs’ supporting cast must step up to compensate for the missing production. De’Aaron Fox is currently averaging 12.4 points, 5.8 assists, and 3.9 rebounds while shooting 47.1% from the field. As the fourth option in scoring behind Wembanyama, Castle, and Harper, his experience could have been pivotal tonight against a frustrated Kings side looking to end their losing ways. The Kings almost beat the Lakers last week (eventually lost 104-106) and subsequently upset the Celtics 97-96 to end their losing streak in the last game. As a result, the shorthanded Spurs side may face a major hurdle tonight without their key players on the floor. Meanwhile, Jordan McLaughlin, who was previously listed as questionable for this game, has been upgraded to available . For the Kings, the players listed out tonight are Ben Simmons (Achilles), Maxime Raynaud (Knee), Sean Pedulla (two-way), and Jonathan Modgo (two-way). Although the Kings have struggled for consistency, their recent win over the Celtics suggests they cannot be taken lightly. It will be interesting to see if they can steal another win tonight against the significantly weakened Spurs roster. With a potential return against the Trail Blazers on Wednesday, November 25, the Spurs will hope this is merely a precautionary absence rather than the beginning of a more concerning injury situation.

item.title: Bruins’ Jeremy Swayman talks giving back, leadership and love for Boston in one-on-one interview
item.description: Boston Bruins goalie Jeremy Swayman says going beyond the game means giving back to the community he plays in. Swayman says it was once a “pipe dream” to play in the NHL, but now he feels deeply connected to Boston. “It was a pipe dream at one point to be in the NHL, but to truly be ingrained into a community like this and a real city that has such heart and soul, I truly feel like I was meant to be here,” he told Boston 25’s Kerry Kavanaugh. He told Kavanaugh people often don’t recognize him without his helmet and pads. But Monday at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, that didn’t much matter. Swayman teamed up with recovery footwear brand OOFOS to donate 350 pairs of shoes to the Dana-Farber breast cancer team as part of OOFOS Project Pink. “I’m just so grateful to be a part of it and the impact that it has on the greater good of people,” Swayman said. He said the donation was about recognizing the people working behind the scenes every day. “The ship doesn’t sail without the hard workers that are here, and I think a little impact that we could do to help their days just go by a little easier and help them do their job to their best ability is something, again, I know you and I would do in a heartbeat.” Nicole Green, chief people officer at OOFOS, said the effort was intended to thank caregivers who can go overlooked. “They’re on their feet all day, and we wanted to give back and say thank you and make them feel good.” Dr. Sara Tolaney, chief of the Division of Breast Oncology at Dana-Farber, said the recognition is meaningful for staff members caring for patients during extraordinarily difficult moments. “Our patients are going through a really challenging time in their lives, and it’s just a nice acknowledgement for the staff to recognize the hard work that they put in every day to make patients get all that they need.” For Swayman, giving back is also part of embracing Boston as home. “It’s everything. It’s ingrained in me now. I feel like I’m a Bostonian and I’m just so grateful to people that have welcomed me with open arms. My entire family, a kid from Alaska, I feel like I really, really do belong here.” That connection carries over to his growing leadership role with the Bruins. Swayman said the best leaders he has encountered have taken the time to understand him as a person, something he wants to pass along to younger teammates. “The greatest leaders I’ve had have wanted to know me for who I am and my background and what I come from. And that’s my favorite thing ever, is digging deep into the human being and learning about them.” Download the FREE Boston 25 News app for breaking news alerts. item.title: Bengals safety Bryan Cook injures ankle vs Commanders Monday night
item.description: Cincinnati Bengals safety Bryan Cook injured his right ankle during the second quarter of the team's NFL Week 11 game against the Washington Commanders on ESPN's Monday Night Football at Northwest Stadium. Cook walked off the field to the sideline under his own power. The Bengals announced that Cook's return is questionable. "It looked like it was gonna be a lot worse," MNF analyst Troy Aikman said during the broadcast. "Definitely a good sign to see him walking off (the field)." Cook was hurt after he was in on a sack of Ravens quarterback Tyler "Snoop" Huntley during the team's NFL Week 7 rout in Baltimore. Cook got up and walked slowly off the field, and returned to the game later in the fourth quarter. Cook hurt his ankle during the first quarter of the team's NFL Week 3 loss in Pittsburgh. Cook missed two games because of the injury. Cook, a former Mount Healthy High School standout and Cincinnati Bearcats defensive back, was on the sideline after having his ankle taped during the Steelers' second scoring drive of the game. Cook returned to the game early in the second quarter. Cook agreed to terms March 9 on a reported three-year deal worth $40.25 million. "My family's been talking about this for a long time," Cook said March 12. "Being able to come back home and … be closer to our family. I'm just excited for the opportunity, excited for the new chapter in my life." Cook was at Kansas City's T-Mobile Center to watch the ninth-seeded Bearcats ' men's basketball team defeat No. 16 seed Utah in the Big 12 tournament. Cook starred at UC from 2019 to 2021 before becoming a second-round pick of the Chiefs in 2022. item.title: SEC threatening vote on LSU expulsion for a second time after RJ Luis drama
item.description: LSU Tigers head coach Will Wade watches his team play against LA Tech Basketball at the Pete Maravich Assembly Center in Baton Rouge, La., Nov. 9, 2026. The SEC is planning to meet on Dec. 3 in order to “decide whether to terminate LSU as an SEC member institution,” the conference revealed on Monday in a legal filing in federal court in Alabama, upping the ante in its ongoing battle with the school. It’s the latest twist in the saga between the conference and the school following LSU’s decision to roster RJ Luis Jr. last week in defiance of the SEC’s rule prohibiting anyone who has signed a pro contract from playing for one of its members’ athletic programs. The conference filed a motion for a temporary restraining order and preliminary injunction against LSU on Monday, revealing plans to consider terminating the school’s membership. LSU guard RJ Luis Jr. (12) shoots against Louisiana Monroe during an NCAA college basketball game in Baton Rouge, La., Wednesday, Nov. 18, 2026. AP Photo/Ella Hall A statement from the SEC read: “The Southeastern Conference on Monday filed an amended complaint and motion for temporary restraining order in its federal lawsuit against Louisiana State University stating that the presidents and chancellors of the SEC will meet on Thursday, December 3, to deliberate LSU’s ongoing membership in the Conference.” “The lawsuit seeks to protect the Conference’s ability to govern itself and to enforce the rules and policies its member universities have voluntarily adopted,” the statement continued. “The Conference maintains its right to associate only with institutions that meet its established standards and expectations of membership and that demonstrate appropriate institutional control of their athletics programs. Monday’s filing advances the Conference’s obligation to defend its governance framework and the shared interests of its member universities.” According to conference rules, at least two-thirds of the 15 other member school presidents would need to vote to terminate LSU’s membership. LSU has not publicly responded to the conference’s move. This is the second time that the SEC has threatened to hold a vote on LSU’s membership, with the first instance coming in a September amended federal complaint stemming from an attempt by LSU’s football team to roster tight end Dae’Quan Wright and defensive lineman Zxavian Harris, both of whom had signed NFL contracts and participated in training camps. item.title: Chandler leads charge in 2nd half as No. 19 BYU rallies past Washington 83-77 at Maui Invitational
item.description: LAHAINIA, HI- NOVEMBER 23: Collin Chandler #5 of the BYU Cougars takes a jump shot over Tayshawn Comer #12 of the Washington Huskies in the second half during a first round Southwest Maui Invitational college basketball game at the Lahaina Civic Center on November 23, 2026 in Lahaina, Hawaii. (Photo by Mitchell Layton/Getty Images) Getty Images LAHINA, Hawaii (AP) — Collin Chandler scored 21 of his game-high 24 points in the second half and No. 19 BYU held off Washington 83-77 Monday on the opening day of the Maui Invitational. The Cougars (6-0) trailed by as many as 15 points in the first half before rallying and turning back the Huskies (4-1). BYU took the lead for good with 5:49 to play on a free throw by Bruce Branch III. After Washington cut it to 66-65 on a jumper by Ryan Beasley, the Cougars answered with an inside bucket by Jaxon Kohler that spurred an 11-4 run that Chandler punctuated with a pair of free throws. That gave BYU its largest lead of the game at 77-69 with 34 seconds remaining. Chandler shot 6 of 12 from the field, including 3 of 6 from 3-point range and was 9 of 10 from the free throw line. Kohler scored 15 points, Tyler Betsey had 13 and Branch 10 for the Cougars, who shot 59.3% (16 of 27) in the second half. LeJuan Watts scored 21 points, Beasley had 20 and Lathan Sommerville chipped in 13 points and nine rebounds for the Huskies. Washington led 29-14 with 8:57 left in the first half after a pair of Beasley free throws. BYU made just 22 of its 36 attempts from the free throw line, while Washington was 23 of 27 from the line. The Huskies drained their first two attempts from beyond the arc — both by Steele Venters — but made only two of their final 16 from distance. The Huskies led at halftime 39-31. BYU played its second straight game without leading scorer Robert Wright III (24.3 points per game). Up next Washington: Faces Clemson in a consolation game Tuesday. BYU: Plays Ole Miss in the semifinal round Tuesday.

item.title: David Bailey already drawing Hall of Fame comparison 10 games into Jets career
item.description: Jets linebacker David Bailey rehabs during practice in Florham Park, N.J., Thursday, Oct. 29, 2026. Demario Davis is in his 15th NFL season, and he has played with some greats. The Jets linebacker sees traits in rookie edge rusher David Bailey that he has observed in some of those great ones. Davis praised Bailey’s “process” on Monday, saying the rookie does not let outside factors affect his preparation routine, similarly to the best players he has been around. “I don’t know what all goes into his process, but I know I see him in the same spots around the building all the time,” Davis said. “That type of stuff is what I’ve seen from guys who are now in the Hall of Fame. When you come in and you go through the week, you see them in the same spots in the building all the time, whether it was an All-Pro wide receiver or an All-Pro running back or an All-Pro quarterback, an All-Pro defensive end in Cam Jordan — a solidified Hall of Famer, one of the best I’ve ever seen do it — it’s all about that process. Those guys have a regimen and a routine that doesn’t change based on what’s going on around them. That’s very rare to see for a rookie.” Jets linebacker David Bailey rehabs during practice in Florham Park, N.J., Thursday, Oct. 29, 2026. Bill Kostroun for NY Post Bailey has been a star on the field. He added two sacks against the Chargers to bring his season total to 9 ½, just shy of Hugh Douglas’ Jets rookie record of 10 set in 1995. He is five away from Jevon Kearse’s NFL rookie record of 14 ½, established in 1999. Davis said Bailey has only scratched the surface of what he can do. “He’s only going to get better,” the veteran linebacker said. “It’s going to be scary for a lot of quarterbacks for a long time and it’s going to be good for the Jets for a long time.” The Jets gave up a touchdown just before halftime Sunday when Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert ran for a 10-yard score as time expired. The Jets showed an interesting defense on the play, with three players rushing and eight players lined up on the goal line. Herbert took off, and the Jets could not bring him down. If they had tackled him, the Chargers might have been unable to even kick a field goal. Both Dane Belton and Davis missed tackles on the play. “They had a chance to try to score on a throwing play and we had guys in the end zone,” head coach Aaron Glenn said, “but then again, if he had a chance to run it, we had guys able to converge on the ball and I think if you look at that play, I think we had two missed tackles, which would’ve put them in a tough situation with six seconds to try to run the ball in that situation. The thing is we just got to make that tackle. We make that tackle; we put ourselves in a good position.”

By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. Croix Bethune, left, celebrates scoring a goal with Kansas City Current teammate Lo’eau LaBonta during an NWSL playoff match in New York, Nov. 15, 2026. I think it was the right decision to come here. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. Another goal conceded, another season to forget. Keisuke Kurokawa's frustration summed up D.C. United's latest disappointing chapter. Scott Taetsch via Getty Images United remains one of three MLS organizations without a developmental team bridging the youth academy to the first team. Efforts to build a complex in Baltimore for an MLS Next Pro operation have floundered. (Meanwhile, United's owners have launched a pro volleyball team.)
